title: Accident-tolerant fuel qualification timelines
bottleneck: Accident-tolerant fuels, coated cladding and doped pellets, promise reactors that survive loss-of-cooling longer, but qualifying new fuel for commercial use requires years of irradiation testing plus post-irradiation examination. Utilities will not load unproven fuel, and test reactors have limited capacity. The payoff in safety margin and longer cycles is real but arrives a decade after development starts. Test reactors that can irradiate full-length fuel rods are scarce and oversubscribed, stretching qualification schedules further.
why_it_blocks: Fuel qualification is nuclear's slowest clock. Every improvement, however valuable, must wait out a decade of irradiation testing, throttling the pace of safety and economic gains.
current_state: Lead test assemblies of coated cladding are irradiating in commercial reactors. Full qualification and batch licensing remain years away.
